units: Is. XLIX, 18,] (sub. בעלת or בת, cmp. אִיתּוּ, חוֹרִים a. בֶּן חוֹרִים) bride; daughter-in-law.
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 1:1">Yeb. I, 1</cite> <he>וכַלָּתוֹ</he> and his (deceased) son’s wife.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 9:14">Sot. IX, 14</cite> <he>שתצא הב׳ וכ׳</he> that the bride on her wedding day may be taken around in procession, v. <cite ref="A02817"><he>אַפִּרְיוֹן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 71b">Keth. 71ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 87a:13">Pes. 87ᵃ</cite> <he>ככ׳ שנמצאת וכ׳</he> like a bride (daughter-in-law) found perfect in the house of her father-in-law.
<cite ref="Pesachim 87a:1">Ib.</cite> <he>כ׳ בבית אביה</he> a bride in her father’s house (not yet taken to her husband’s paternal house).

Ex. R. s. 41 (play on ככלתו, Ex. XXXI, 18, cmp. כְּלַל Pa.) מה כ׳ זו מקושטת וכ׳ as the bride is adorned &c.; a. fr. [Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 18 כ׳ נופי, read with ed. Bub. ib. 9 קלי נינפי.]—Pl. כַּלּוֹת. Sot. l. c. עטרות כ׳ (Talm. ed. sing.) the bridal wreaths. Ib. 49ᵇ; a. fr

senses.gloss: general assembly, esp. Kallah, the assembly of Babylonian students in the months of Elul and Adar.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 8b:3">Ber. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>פרשייתא דכ׳</he> Ar. (Ms. Paris <he>דכַלָּא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S., Vol. I, p. 384; ed. <he>דכולא שתא</he>) the weekly Scripture lessons of the Kallah weeks (during which R. Bibi could not find time to peruse the section of each week). Ib. 6ᵃ, v. <cite ref="D00231"><he>דּוּחֲקָא</he></cite>. Ib. 57ᵃ <he>ראש לבני כ׳</he>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 22a:10">B. Bath. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>ריש כ׳</he> the president of the Kallah.—Pl. (of <cite ref="K00716"><he>כַּלָּא</he></cite>) <cite ref="K00716"><he>כַּלֵּי</he></cite>.
Ḥull. 49ᵃ רישי כ׳.—מסכת כלה, מסכתא דכ׳ a (small) treatise of the Talmud named Kallah (from its first word).

<cite ref="Shabbat 114a:7">Sabb. 114ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Kiddushin 49b:2">Kidd. 49ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Taanit 10b:2">Taan. 10ᵇ</cite>; [oth. opin.: a subject which has been discussed in the general assembly].
